summary: Noah builds a wooden ark that carries his household and animals on the floodwaters. Moses’ mother places him in a small vessel of papyrus among the reeds at the Nile’s edge.

senses.definition: A vessel built to keep its occupants afloat on water.

evidence.note: Living creatures come to Noah in pairs and enter הַתֵּבָה.
Moses’ mother coats a papyrus basket with bitumen and pitch, puts the child inside, and sets it among the reeds at the riverbank.
Noah and his family enter the ark, and the animals go in to him.
Noah is to make a תֵּבָה of wood with compartments and coat it inside and out with pitch.
Noah is to make the ark of gopher wood, divide it into compartments, and coat it inside and out with pitch.
Noah is told to make a תֵּבָה of wood, divide it into compartments, and coat it inside and out with pitch.
Noah is told to make the ark of wood, divide it into compartments, and coat it inside and out with pitch.
Noah reaches out, takes the dove, and brings her into the ark.
Noah, his family, and the animals enter the ark, and the rising waters lift it above the ground.
The dove finds nowhere to rest her foot. In וַתָּשָׁב אֵלָיו אֶל הַתֵּבָה, she returns to Noah, and אֶל הַתֵּבָה identifies her destination as the ark.
The increasing waters lift the ark above the ground.
The rising waters lift the ark, and it floats on the surface.
The creatures with Noah are identified as those who came out of the ark.

אֹרֶךְ הַתֵּבָה gives the ark’s length as 300 cubits. The feminine singular suffixes in רָחְבָּהּ “its width” and קוֹמָתָהּ “its height” refer back to the same vessel, whose width and height are 50 and 30 cubits.
